Date: 2021-12-08
REMARKS
Claims 21, 23-27, 29, 31-37, and 39-50 are pending. Claim 21 is amended. Support for the claim amendments may be found in the as-filed claims and specification; e.g., at [0039]- [0041]. Claims 1-20 and 22 were previously cancelled. Claims 28, 30, and 38 are cancelled without prejudice to, or disclaimer of, the underlying subject matter. Applicant expressly reserves the right to file the subject matter of any cancelled claims in a later continuation application. No new matter enters by way of the present amendment. Entry of the amendment and reconsideration of the application based on the following remarks is respectfully requested.
I. Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103
A. Claims 21, 23-26, 29, and 37
The Examiner rejects claims 21, 23-26, 29, and 37 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over US Publication 2016/0338591 to Lachenbruch et al. ("Lachenbruch") in view of US Publication 2015/0186607 to Geleijnse et al. ("Geleijnse"). See Office Action at 4. Specifically, the Examiner alleges that "Lachenbruch et al. teaches a method of providing a continuity of care for a patient at risk of developing pressure ulcers (PU) during transfer from a first care setting to a second care setting, the method comprising the steps of: making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting. . . calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements... determining whether the delta value exceeds a threshold... do nothing if the delta value does not exceed the threshold. . . do something if the delta value exceeds the threshold. " Id. at 4-5. The Examiner concedes that Lachenbruch "does not explicitly teach a current intervention as well as the optionality to change the intervention based on the measurements." Id. at 5. However, the Examiner cites Geleijnse for providing "identifying a current PU intervention of level-K received by the patient at the first care setting. . . wherein the current PU intervention of level-K is provided in a transfer record. . . do nothing by continuing to administer the current PU intervention. . . do something by administering a new PU intervention of level-N, where N has a value greater than K." Id. at 6. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time of the invention was filed would have found it obvious to 1) identify a current PU intervention of level-K received by the patient at the first care setting, wherein the current PU intervention of level-K is provided in a transfer record, 2) continue to administer the current PU intervention, and 3) administer a new PU intervention of level-N, where N has a value greater than K as taught by Geleseijnse [sic] et al. in the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al. with the motivation(s) of monitoring a patient's condition and adjusting the level of care accordingly." Id. at 6-7.
At the outset, without acquiescing to the rejection, and solely to advance prosecution, Applicant amends claim 21 to recite "each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance."
"The key to supporting any rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) is the clear articulation of the reason(s) why the claimed invention would have been obvious.... [R]ejections on obviousness cannot be sustained with mere conclusory statements." MPEP § 2142. "[T]he framework for the objective analysis for determining obviousness under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) is stated in Graham v. John Deere Co., 383 U.S. 1, 148 USPQ 459 (1966).... The factual inquiries ... [include determining the scope and content of the prior art and] ... [a]scertaining the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art." MPEP § 2141(11). In rejecting a claim, "Office personnel must explain why the difference(s) between the prior art and the claimed invention would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art." MPEP § 2141(11). Here, no primafacie case of obviousness has been established, for at least the reason that the Office has not (1) properly determined the scope and content of the prior art, (2) properly ascertained the differences between the prior art and the claimed subject matter, or (3) demonstrated a motivation to combine the cited references.
1. Scope and content of Lachenbruch
Applicant submits that the Office has not properly determined the scope and content of Lachenbruch.
The Examiner cites Lachenbruch and alleges that it provides "calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements." Office Action at 4. For support, the Examiner alleges Lachenbruch for providing "one or more sensors 102 are positioned to collect or sense information regarding a tissue status for the individual. . . the sensor collects information regarding subepidermal moisture (SEM) levels as a measure of impedance in dermal phase units (DPU). . . ." Lachenbruch at [0037]. However, the Examiner then deviates from Lachenbruch, by further alleging that:
"Impedance is also a measure of flow, thus it is measured using two points in order to determine the flow. An individual sensor itself would therefore include two measurements points in order to calculate the impedance. Accordingly the measurement of an impedance itself is a delta value."
Office Action at 4-5.
Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's characterization of impedance. "[W]hile 'common sense' can be invoked, even potentially to supply a limitation missing from the prior art, it must still be supported by evidence and a reasoned explanation.... [T]his is particularly true where the missing limitation goes to the heart of an invention." Arendi v. Apple, 832 F.3d 1355, 1363 (Fed. Cir. 2016). Beyond mere conclusory statements, the Examiner has not provided evidence or a reasoned explanation for his assertion that the measurement of an impedance is itself a delta value. Applicant respectfully submits that the measurement of impedance is a complex quantity and is not merely a difference between measurements made at two measurement points, whatever the variable of measurement may be. See e.g., Electrical Impedance, Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical impedance (last visited November 6, 2021). Accordingly, the Examiner has not made aprimafacie showing that the measurement of impedance itself is a delta value.
2. Differences between Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and the instant claims Applicant submits that the Examiner also has not properly ascertained the differences between the prior art and the claimed subject matter. In particular, Applicant submits that contrary to the Examiner's allegations, neither Lachenbruch nor Geleijnse provide "making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance," and "calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements," as recited in amended claim 21.
As amended, claim 21 recites that each SEM measurement comprises a measurement of biocapacitance. The as-filed disclosure also provides that "'delta' refers to a calculated difference between two SEM values." Specification at [0050] (emphasis added). As explained in Section 1 above, the Examiner has not shown that Lachenbruch provides measurement of impedance it itself a delta value. Whatever Lachenbruch allegedly provides, it does not provide "making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance," and "calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements," as recited in amended claim 21.
Geleijnse was allegedly cited for providing "identifying a current PU intervention of level-K received by the patient at the first care setting," "do nothing by continuing to administer the current PU intervention," and "do something by administering a new PU intervention of level-N, where N has a value greater than K." However, Geleijnse does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch. That is, it also does not provide "making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance," and "calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements," as recited in amended claim 21.
Applicant respectfully submits that since neither Lachenbruch nor Geleijnse, whether alone or in combination, provide each and every element of amended claim 21, the Examiner has not made aprimafacie showing of obviousness.
3. No motivation to combine Lachenbruch and Gelijnse; Improper hindsight used
Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner has not made a primafacie showing that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine the teachings of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse. The Examiner indicates that "[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time of the invention was filed would have found it obvious to 1) identify a current PU intervention of level-K received by the patient at the first care setting, wherein the current PU intervention of level-K is provided in a transfer record, 2) continue to administer the current PU intervention, and 3) administer a new PU intervention of level-N, where N has a value greater than K as taught by Gelesenijnse et al. in the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al. with the motivation(s) of monitoring a patient's condition and adjusting the level of care accordingly (see: paragraph [0002] of Geleijnse et al.)." Office Action at 7-8.
Applicant respectfully disagrees with this characterization of Geleijnse. Geleijnse, at best, provides a clinical support system and a corresponding clinical support method. Geleijnse at Abstract. Geleijnse also provides a computer-readable storage medium that contains "instructions for execution by the processor, wherein the instructions cause the processor to perform the steps of obtaining current patient data descriptive of a patient, for whom a recommendation for a transition from a current care levels to one or more other care levels shall be provided, in the current care level, obtaining historic patient data of the patient obtained earlier in the current and/or other care levels." Id. However, Geleijnse does not provide this in the context of skin indications, much less pressure ulcer. Amended claim 1 recites "identifying a current PU intervention of level-K received by the patient at the first care setting, wherein the current PU intervention of level-K is provided in a transfer record. . . continuing to administer the current PU intervention if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, and administering a new PU intervention of level-N if the delta value exceeds the threshold, where N has a value greater than K." Applicant respectfully submits that one of ordinary skill in the art would not have been motivated to combine Geleijnse with Lachenbruch, at least because Geleijnse is silent on administering any interventions for pressure ulcers or skin conditions. The Examiner otherwise has not established that elsewhere in the art provides motivation to modify Geleijnse with Lachenbruch. As such, any motivation to combine the references must have been reconstructed from the Examiner's understanding of the Applicant's disclosure. Since any motivation to combine the Geleijnse with the rest of the cited references can only be in view of the Applicant's disclosure, Applicant submits that the Examiner appears to be using impermissible hindsight to improperly interpret the claimed subject matter as obvious over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse.
Applicant submits that amended claim 21 is not obvious over Lachenbruch and Geleijnse, and Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw his rejection of amended claim 21. Claims 23-26, 29, and 37 depend from claim 21. Dependent claims are nonobvious under 35 U.S.C. § 103 if the independent claims from which they depend are nonobvious. See e.g., In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Thus, claims 23-26, 29, and 37 are also nonobvious.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claims 21, 23-26, 29, and 37 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse.
B. Claim 27
The Examiner rejects claim 27 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of U.S. Patent 9,028,407 to Bennet- Guerrero ("Bennet-Guerrero"). See Office Action at 12. Specifically, the Examiner alleges that Bennet Guerrero provides "continuing to make a plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, and making a plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-N if the delta value exceeds the threshold." Id. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Bennet-Guerrero provides an apparatus for monitoring patient orientation.
Bennett-Guerrero at Abstract. However, whatever Bennet-Guerrero provides, it does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse, as discussed in Subsection A above. Bennet- Guerrrero does not provide or suggest at least making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance, and calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, as recited in amended claim 21. Accordingly, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Bennet-Guerrero, whether alone or in combination do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Claim 27 depends from claim 21, and as such, is also non-obvious over these references by virtue of its dependence from amended claim 21.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claim 27 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, and further in view of Bennet-Guerrero.
C. Claims 28, 30, and 38
The Examiner rejects claims 28, 30, and 38 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of US Publication 2017/0007153 to Tonar et al. ("Tonar"). Office Action at 13. Without acquiescing to the rejection, and solely to advance prosecution, Applicant cancels claims 28, 30, and 38, without prejudice to, or disclaimer of, the underlying subject matter. Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection claims 28, 30, and 38 is moot by virtue of their cancellation.
D. Claims 31, 32, 34, and 39
The Examiner rejects claims 31, 32, 34, and 39 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of US Patent 9,675,289 to Heaton ("Heaton"). Office Action at 16. Specifically for claim 31, the Examiner alleges that Heaton provides "querying the database for data to form retrieved data values (see FIG. 9 where there is a directory for storing and retrieving archived responses into and from the database. In order for the system here to access the database here, it would query the database in order to retrieve the necessary data)." Office Action at 17. As such, the Examiner concludes that "[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time the invention was filed would have found it obvious to query the database for data to form retrieved delta values as taught by Heaton in the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al. and Gele[]ijnse et al. in combination with the motivation(s) of being a way to store and retrieve information from a database." Id. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Heaton at best provides "[a] system and method for monitoring individual metabolic response and for generating nutritional feedback involve monitoring of a glucose level in a qualified subject." Heaton at Abstract. Whatever Heaton does provide, it does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse, as discussed in Subsection A above. Heaton does not provide or suggest at least making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance, and calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, as recited in amended claim 21. Accordingly, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Heaton, whether alone or in combination do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Claim 31, 32, 34, and 39 depend from claim 21, and as such, are also non-obvious over these references by virtue of its dependence from amended claim 21.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claims 31, 32, 34, and 39 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Heaton.
E. Claim 33
The Examiner rejects claim 33 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of US Publication 2008/0015894 to Miller et al. ("Miller"). Office Action at 19. Specifically, the Examiner alleges that Miller provides "creating an additional data record, wherein the data element comprises one or more of a nutritional information, an implemented intervention, a risk assessment, a visual skin assessment, a care plan, a doctor's note, an event, a vital sign, a body weight, and a lab result," and "reporting the additional data record to the database." Id. at 20. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time of the invention was filed would have found it obvious to 1) create an additional data record, wherein the data element comprises. . . and 2) report the additional data record to the database as taught by Miller et al. in the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al. and Gele[]ijnse et al. in combination with the motivation(s) of updating a patient files." Id. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Miller, at best, provides "[a] method of assessing a health risk associated with a medication therapy regimen identifies potentially adverse health outcomes resulting from the medication therapy regimen." Miller at Abstract. Whatever Miller does provide, it does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse, as discussed in Subsection A above. Heaton does not provide or suggest at least making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance, and calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, as recited in amended claim 21. Accordingly, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Miller, whether alone or in combination do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Claim 33 depends from claim 21, and as such, are also non-obvious over these references by virtue of its dependence from amended claim 21.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claim 33 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Miller.
F. Claims 35 and 36
The Examiner rejects claims 35 and 36 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Heaton, and further in view of US Patent 8,355,925 to Rothman et al. ("Rothman"). Office Action at 20-21.
Specifically, the Examiner alleges that Rothman provides "the step of analyzing the retrieved values to determine one or more of a slope, an acceleration, a curve shape and associated characteristics, and a time-to-intercept of a selected threshold." Id. at 21. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time [of] the invention was filed would have found it obvious to have the step of analyzing the retrieved values to determine one or more of a slope, an acceleration, a curve shape and associated characteristics, and a time-to-intercept of a selected threshold as taught by Rothman et al. in the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al., Gele[]ijnse et al., and Heaton in combination with the motivation(s) of alerting a user if a patient is getting better or worse at an accelerating rate." Id. at 21-22. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Rothman at best provides "methods of assessing risk based on medical data and uses thereof, and more particularly, to deriving functions for assessing risk associated with medical data." Rothman at col. 1 lines 14-17. Whatever Rothman does provide, it does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Heaton, as discussed in Subsection D above. Rothman does not provide or suggest at least making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance, and calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, as recited in amended claim 21. Accordingly, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Heaton, and Rothman, whether alone or in combination do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Claim 35 and 36 depend from claim 21, and as such, are also non-obvious over these references by virtue of its dependence from amended claim 21.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claims 35 and 36 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Heaton, and further in view of Rothman.
G. Claims 40 and 43
The Examiner rejects claims 40 and 43 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of "Protocol for the successful treatment of pressure ulcers" to Brem et al. ("Brem"). Office Action at 22.
Specifically, the Examiner alleges that Brem provides "wherein a level-0 PU intervention is selected from the group consisting of providing good nutrition, standard mattress, turning ever 24 hours, and a combination thereof," and "a level-3 PU intervention of applying dressing to the back or sides of patient's heel." Id. at 23-24. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "it would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to substitute a group consisting of providing good nutrition, standard mattress, turning every 24 hours, and a combination thereof as taught by Brem et al. for the group as disclosed by Lachenbruch et al and Gele[]ijnse et al. in combination since each individual element and its function are shown in the prior art, with the difference being the substitution of the elements."
Id. at 23. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Brem provides, at best, a 12-step protocol for treatment of pressure ulcers. Brem at Abstract. Brem is silent on providing good nutrition, standard mattress, turning every 24 hours, and any combination thereof as a level-0 PU intervention, or applying dressing to the back or sides of patient's heel as a level-3 PU intervention. At a minimum, the Examiner has not provided any rationale to modify and designate Brem's intervention methods as a level-0 or a level-3 PU intervention, as opposed to other intervention levels. Further, whatever Brem provides, it does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse, as discussed in Subsection A above. Brem does not provide or suggest at least making a plurality of Sub- Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance, and calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, as recited in amended claim 21. Accordingly, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Brem, whether alone or in combination do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Claim 40 and 43 depend from claim 21, and as such, are also non-obvious over these references by virtue of its dependence from amended claim 21.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claims 40 and 43 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Brem.
H. Claim 41
The Examiner rejects claim 41 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of US Patent 5,367,789 to Lamont ("Lamont"). Office Action at 24. Specifically, the Examiner alleges that Lamont provides a level-1 PU intervention of providing a heel boot to the patient. Id. at 24. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "it would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to substitute a level-1 PU intervention of providing a heel boot to the patient as taught by Lamont for a treatment level as disclosed by Lachenbruch et al and Gele[]ijnse et al. in combination since each individual element and its function are shown in the prior art, with the difference being the substitution of the elements." Id. at 25. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Lamont provides, at best, a soft medical boot having an articulated splint bar for adjusting the angle of the foot of a patient dispose in a supine position. Lamont at Abstract. Lamont is silent on applying its soft medical boot as a level-1 PU intervention. At a minimum, the Examiner has not provided any rationale to modify and designate Lamont's soft medical boot as a level-1 PU intervention, as opposed to other intervention levels. Furthermore, whatever Lamont provides, it does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse, as discussed in Subsection A above. Lamont does not provide or suggest at least making a plurality of Sub- Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance, and calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, as recited in amended claim 21. Accordingly, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Lamont, whether alone or in combination do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Claim 41 depends from claim 21, and as such, is also non-obvious over these references by virtue of its dependence from amended claim 21.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claim 41 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Lamont.
. Claim 42
The Examiner rejects claim 42 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of US Patent 6,634,045 to DuDonis et al.
("DuDonis"). Office Action at 25. Specifically, the Examiner alleges that DuDonis provides "a level-2 PU intervention of changing the patient's support surface." Id. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "it would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to substitute a level-2 PU intervention of changing the patient's support surface as taught by DuDonis for a treatment level as disclosed by Lachenbruch et al and Gele[]ijnse et al. in combination since each individual element and its function are shown in the prior art, with the difference being the substitution of the elements." Id. at 26. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
DuDonis provides, at best, a heel elevating foam cushion is used to relieve heel pressure ulcers in patients confined to bed. DuDonis at Abstract. DuDonis is silent on changing the patient's support surface as a level-2 PU intervention. At a minimum, the Examiner has not provided any rationale to modify and designate DuDonis's intervention methods as a level-2 PU intervention, as opposed to other intervention levels. Further, whatever DuDonis provides, it does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse, as discussed in Subsection A above. DuDonis does not provide or suggest making at least a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance, and calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, as recited in amended claim 21. Accordingly, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and DuDonis, whether alone or in combination do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Claim 42 depends from claim 21, and as such, is also non-obvious over these references by virtue of its dependence from amended claim 21.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claim 42 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of DuDonis.
J. Claim 44
The Examiner rejects claim 44 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of "Friction between human skin and medical textiles for decubitus prevention" to Rotaru et al. ("Rotaru"). Office Action at p. 26.
Specifically, the Examiner alleges that Rotaru provides a level-4 PU intervention of changing the patient's sheet cover to a low-friction sheet cover. Id. at 27. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "it would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to substitute a level-4 PU intervention of changing the patient's sheet cover to a low-friction sheet cover as taught by Rotaru, for a treatment program of a certain diagnostic level as disclosed by Lachenbruch et al and Gele[]ijnse et al. in combination since each individual element and its function are shown in the prior art, with the difference being the substitution of the elements." Id. at 27. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Rotaru provides, at best, that risk of pressure ulcers could be reduced by improved hospital bedsheets. Rotaru at Abstract. Rotaru is silent on providing changing the patient's sheet cover to a low-friction sheet cover as a level-4 PU intervention. At a minimum, the Examiner has not provided any rationale to modify and designate Rotaru's intervention methods as a level- 4 PU intervention, as opposed to other intervention levels. Further, whatever Rotaru provides, it does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse, as discussed in Subsection A above. Rotaru does not provide or suggest making at least a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance, and calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, as recited in amended claim 21.
Accordingly, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Rotaru, whether alone or in combination do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Claim 44 depends from claim 21, and as such, is also non-obvious over these references by virtue of its dependence from amended claim 21.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claim 44 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Rotaru.
K. Claim 45
The Examiner rejects claim 45 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of US Patent 8,011,041 to Hann ("Hann"). Office Action at 27. Specifically, the Examiner alleges that Hann provides "a level-5 PU intervention of providing a low-friction padded mattress surface for the patient's lower leg."
Id. at 28. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "it would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to substitute a level-5 PU intervention of providing a low-friction padded mattress surface for the patient's lower leg as taught by Hann for a treatment program of a certain diagnostic level as disclosed by Lachenbruch et al and Gele[]ijnse et al. in combination since each individual element and its function are shown in the prior art, with the difference being the substitution of the elements."
Id. at 28. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Hann provides, at best, a multi-layered textile assembly that possesses qualities that are important for reducing the risk of pressure sore formation through improved comfort, moisture wicking, breathability, shear reducing, rapid drying and anti-microbial, while being durable, launderable and lightweight. Hann at col. 3 lines 23-29. Hann is silent on providing a low- friction padded mattress surface for the patient's lower leg as a level-5 PU intervention. At a minimum, the Examiner has not provided any rationale to modify and designate Hann's intervention methods as a level-5 PU intervention, as opposed to other intervention levels.
Further, whatever Hann provides, it does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse, as discussed in Subsection A above. Hann does not provide or suggest at least making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, each SEM measurement comprising a measurement of biocapacitance, and calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, as recited in amended claim 21. Accordingly, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Hann, whether alone or in combination do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Claim 45 depends from claim 21, and as such, is also non-obvious over these references by virtue of its dependence from amended claim 21.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claim 45 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Hann.
L. Claims 46 and 47
The Examiner rejects claims 46 and 47 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of "Prevention and Treatment of Pressure Ulcers" to Thomas ("Thomas"). Office Action at 28-29.
